vegetable.status: experimental; retained after candidate negative-example regression

board.status: experimental, improved on real kitchen scenes; default board model for check_board_misuse.py
board.why_not_default_food: not a food model; board localisation only
board.change_vs_baseline: fine-tuned from board_baseline with 2 verified real boards and 44 verified no-board kitchen scenes
limitations: Precision 0.44 on real kitchen photos is better but still far from usable for automatic judgement.
Recall on real kitchens is unmeasured.
Hold-out is 92 Open Images kitchen photos, not canteen footage.

evaluated_alternatives.name: board_v3_real (second labelling batch, 284 train images)
evaluated_alternatives.verdict: not promoted: board test mAP50 0.897 vs 0.912, precision 0.902 vs 0.933, and more detections on the fresh 90-image kitchen probe (39 vs 32 boxes)

board.data_status: Open Images cutting-board images are exhausted: all 196 train / 10 validation / 24 test images have been used. Further public-data experiments would reuse the same photos, so the only meaningful next step is self-shot kitchen or canteen photos.

foodseg.status: experimental, best model so far; opt-in via --food-model foodseg; NOT the default
foodseg.why_not_default: Trained on FoodSeg103 dish photos plus 156 empty board photos, never on real kitchen footage. Its numbers come from dish photography, so treat them as an upper bound for a real 后厨.
foodseg.dataset: foodseg_two_class (FoodSeg103, processed_meat merged into meat, + 156 background boards)

board_only_probe.note: 2 of the 3 raw detections were on probe images that actually contain food

policy_alias_notes: meat covers steak/pork/chicken-duck/lamb plus sausage/fried meat from FoodSeg103
processed_meat was merged into meat because it was not learnable at this data size
FoodSeg103 has no raw-vs-cooked annotation: do not read 生熟 out of this model

previous_entries.verdict: superseded: three classes cost 0.17 mAP50; merging processed_meat into meat lifted mAP50 0.416 to 0.591 and recall 0.368 to 0.424, at the price of one audited bare-board false positive
superseded: 156 background boards removed bare-board false positives (7/22 to 0/22 at conf 0.5) at a small cost to mAP50 (0.435 to 0.416)

food_type.status: experimental research model; opt-in only via --food-model food_type; NOT the default
food_type.why_not_default: Fixed-confidence recall is very low (0.092 at conf 0.50 on 220 test images) and 10 of 22 board-only weak-negative images produced at least one detection. The legacy vegetable model remains the default.

evaluated_alternatives.name: food_taxonomy_v2 (background boards)
evaluated_alternatives.verdict: not promoted: board-only false positives fell 10/22 to 3/22 but test mAP50-95 dropped 0.0228

evaluated_alternatives.name: food_taxonomy_v3 (third class other_food + 120 backgrounds)
evaluated_alternatives.verdict: not promoted: other_food works (AP50 0.566) and held-out bread is now correct, but animal_food AP50 fell 0.320 to 0.144 and cheese matched recall fell 11.2% to 0.9% at conf 0.50

evaluated_alternatives.name: food_taxonomy_v4s (YOLO11s on the v3 data)
evaluated_alternatives.verdict: not promoted: 3.6x parameters did not recover animal_food (AP50 0.144 to 0.138, cheese 0.9% to 6.0%), so capacity is not the bottleneck

open_findings: At conf 0.50 the detector is far from usable: per-subtype hit rates are 1-40% for everything except hamburger/bread/doughnut.
animal_food is not one visual class (egg 0.585 vs seafood 0.203 at conf 0.25 in v1). Splitting it into seafood and egg_dairy is the next class change.
The 0.50 operating point was never calibrated. A threshold sweep on existing test data is the cheapest next step.

precision_first.status: current default; kept because the rule engine is an alerting tool where false alarms cost more

recall_first.status: available via --food-confidence 0.25; needs more human review capacity

calibrated_thresholds.finding: No threshold makes the detector usable: best F1 is about 0.30 at conf 0.10-0.20, and per-class only other_food reaches a workable point (P 0.744 / R 0.408 at conf 0.50). The bottleneck is detection quality, not the threshold.
calibrated_thresholds.caveat: Calibrated on the food_taxonomy_v1 validation split (139 images) and confirmed on its 220-image test split, both public-data, not kitchen data.

board_lvis.status: experimental opt-in only; not promoted because predefined absolute criteria were not all met
limitations: Public LVIS/COCO photos new to board-label development, not canteen footage.
Only 38 test images, 15 positive and 23 explicitly negative.
23 source images come from COCO train2017; generic YOLO pretraining may have seen them for other classes. No globally unseen-image claim.
Historical test used only as a predefined regression guard, not independent performance evidence.
Photo/source filtering does not prove independent households or scenes.
